gates.G10_the_three_cell_test_and_its_limits: PRE-REGISTERED. urls[4], urls[5] and urls[6] are the analyst's 0819-R5 proposal, adopted whole. Three URLs already in the corpus, fired in ONE run so client and instant are held constant: urls[4] the Hela Schwarz PDF whose 403 the 2026-06-30 and 2026-07-01 records report through an instrument that no longer exists; urls[5] a /sites/ .pdf this relay served ok/200 on 2026-08-18; urls[6] a /cases/ path this relay was refused 403 on 2026-08-18. WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO, STATED FIRST: it does NOT separate the /sites/ prefix hypothesis from the .pdf extension hypothesis. 0819-R2 shows that is impossible from this corpus - the two are PERFECTLY CONFOUNDED across all 73 italaw URLs the project has ever held, with zero members in each of the two cells that would separate them - and 0819-R3 shows the static-file hypothesis is not separable even in principle by this instrument. I adopt both findings. WHAT IT DOES: it tests whether path shape was ever the right variable. IF urls[4] RETURNS 200: the July 403 was a client-or-date effect, not a path effect, and path shape survives as a candidate. IF urls[4] RETURNS 403 WHILE urls[5] RETURNS 200: two members of the SAME cell diverge inside ONE run with client and instant held constant, and path shape is REFUTED as sufficient. IF BOTH urls[4] AND urls[5] RETURN 403: the 2026-08-18 finding is not reproducible a day later and the whole path frame is a time effect. Every one of those readings is bounded by G5 and none is a statement about italaw's policy.
